about.title: Galt Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Galt sees its share of crashes on the corridors that carry the most daily traffic — SR-99, A Street, Twin Cities Road, and C Street. Recent public records show dozens of injury collisions here each year, with Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. showing up often in the count. When one of these crashes happens to you, the aftermath can feel disorienting: medical appointments, missed work, and an insurance adjuster who calls sooner than you'd expect. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves — we're a free service that connects injured Galt residents with an independent personal injury attorney who takes cases on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless money is recovered. Our role is simple: help you find someone who can look at your specific situation, explain your options under California law, and take some of that pressure off your shoulders while you focus on healing.

whyChoose.title: Why Galt Residents Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: California's Filing Clock Moves Fast
items.desc: You generally have two years to file a car accident claim in California, but if a government vehicle or road defect was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. Talking to an attorney early helps make sure a deadline doesn't quietly pass while you're still recovering.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work Against You If You're Not Careful
items.desc: California allows you to recover damages even if you're partly at fault, but your share of fault reduces what you can collect. An early conversation with an attorney can help you avoid saying something to an insurer that gets used to inflate your share of blame.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Damages Means Details Matter
items.desc: California doesn't limit compensation for pain, suffering, or loss of enjoyment of life in most car accident cases, so how your injuries and their impact are documented matters. Connecting with an attorney soon after a crash on A Street or Twin Cities Road helps preserve that evidence while it's still fresh.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally wise to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurance adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to minimize your claim later. An independent attorney can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: What if my accident happened on SR-99 near Galt during a busy Friday afternoon?
items.answer: Crashes on higher-traffic corridors like SR-99 often involve multiple vehicles and more complex evidence, especially during peak hours. Acting quickly to document the scene, get medical care, and speak with an attorney can help preserve details that matter for your claim.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No, our service is free. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation, so there's no upfront cost to you either way.
